title: Exam Orientation and How to Study

header.html: Exam overview, domain map and answer technique (all domains)
Know the exam format and the five domains with their weights; know the question types including performance-based questions; use a repeatable method to answer every question
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1The exam at a glance

Item Fact
Exam code N10-009 (version 9)
Questions A maximum of 90
Question types Multiple-choice and performance-based (simulations)
Time 90 minutes
Passing score 720 on a scale of 100 to 900
Recommended experience 9 to 12 months in the IT networking field
Lifecycle Launched June 20, 2024; CompTIA exams usually retire about three years after launch (estimated 2027) [Verify live]
Exam tip

. Performance-based questions come first. They are simulations (drag and drop, configure a device, read a diagram). They take longer, so flag them and return if you are short of time, but do not skip them.

2The five domains

Domain Weight Objectives
1.0 Networking Concepts 23% 1.1 to 1.8
2.0 Network Implementation 20% 2.1 to 2.4
3.0 Network Operations 19% 3.1 to 3.5
4.0 Network Security 14% 4.1 to 4.3
5.0 Network Troubleshooting 24% 5.1 to 5.5
Exam tip

. Troubleshooting (24%) and concepts (23%) together are almost half the exam. Learn the troubleshooting method and the ports, protocols and subnetting cold.

3How to answer every question

  1. Read the last line to see what is asked.
  2. Identify the OSI layer or the device the scenario points to.
  3. Eliminate options that belong to a different layer or a different protocol.
  4. Choose the simplest explanation that fits all the facts.
  5. Answer every question; never leave a blank.

CompTIA lists acronyms the exam may use; this course spells every acronym out the first time.

4A study plan

Phase Modules Goal
1 1 to 7 Concepts: OSI, appliances, cloud, ports, media, subnetting
2 8 to 11 Implementation: routing, switching, wireless, racks
3 12 to 16 Operations: documentation, monitoring, DR, services, access
4 17 to 19 Security
5 20 to 25 Troubleshooting and final practice

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1What is the passing score for the N10-009 exam?

  • A700 on a scale of 100 to 900
  • B720 on a scale of 100 to 900
  • C750 on a scale of 100 to 1,000
  • D800 on a scale of 100 to 900
Show the answer

Answer: B. The passing score is 720 on a scale of 100 to 900.

S2A candidate meets a long simulation question at the start of the exam. What is the best approach?

  • ASkip it permanently because simulations are unscored
  • BFlag it, answer the quicker questions, and return to the simulation
  • CSpend half of the exam time on it right away
  • DAnswer it randomly and move on without review
Show the answer

Answer: B. Performance-based questions are scored, but taking them later saves time for the rest.

S3Which two domains together carry the largest share of the exam?

  • ANetwork Security and Network Operations
  • BNetwork Implementation and Network Security
  • CNetwork Troubleshooting and Networking Concepts
  • DNetwork Operations and Network Implementation
Show the answer

Answer: C. Troubleshooting (24 percent) and concepts (23 percent) are the two largest.

S4How many questions can the exam contain at most?

  • A60
  • B75
  • C90
  • D100
Show the answer

Answer: C. The exam has a maximum of 90 questions.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the exam code?

Show the answer

N10-009.

R2How long is the exam?

Show the answer

90 minutes.

R3Name the two question types.

Show the answer

Multiple-choice and performance-based.

R4Which domain has the highest weight?

Show the answer

Network Troubleshooting, at 24 percent.

R5What is the lowest domain weight?

Show the answer

Network Security, at 14 percent.

R6How much networking experience does CompTIA recommend?

Show the answer

9 to 12 months.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Format up to 90 questions, 90 minutes, 720 of 900, multiple-choice and performance-based
Weights 23 / 20 / 19 / 14 / 24 percent
Method find the layer or device, eliminate, pick the simplest fit
Simulations flag and return; never skip
